text: {"final": {"verdict": "reject", "reason": "The code contradicts the finding. There is no send_sms(phone, text) function in notifications/sms.py; the sending function is queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params, *, now=None) -> SmsMessage, which takes a household ID plus a template ID and params, not a raw phone/text. It raises RuntimeError if feature('sms_enabled') is False and ValueError if the rendered text exceeds MAX_LENGTH (via render), but it also raises ValueError if the household has not agreed to SMS (household.sms_ok). The appended record is a SmsMessage with keys id, household_id, phone, template_id, params, text, queued_at — not exactly the keys id, phone, text, queued_at. queued_at does use (now or _now()).isoformat(timespec='seconds') and the record is appended to data/outbox/sms.jsonl, so those parts are correct, but the function name, signature, and record shape are wrong."}}
reasoning: The finding claims send_sms(phone, text, *, now=None) exists. The actual function is queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params, *, now=None). No send_sms function. Also record keys differ: SmsMessage has id, household_id, phone, template_id, params, text, queued_at. So the finding is wrong.
